macro.story:
The tape is in a constructive bull regime: SPY at 750 sits +9.5% above its 200-day moving average, the Russell 2000 is participating with a fresh MACD bullish crossover, and 8 of 11 GICS sectors trade above their 50-day. The VIX collapsed -26% in five days back to 16.3, and Engine C reads CALM — no washout, no euphoric extreme, just normal trend conditions where rotation and stock-picking work. This is a 'where to hunt' market, not a 'rescue the index' market.

The dominant catalyst grounded in the active theme data is the AI Infrastructure capex cycle in its CHASING stage, paired with the Geopolitical Risk Unwind around Iran/Hormuz. Crude is down 30% over 21 days and sits at oversold extremes (RSI 30) — that supply-side relief is unambiguously risk-on, compressing CPI expectations and feeding capital into equities. You can see the rotation footprint clearly: gold and silver are down 4–9% over 21 days as the inflation-hedge bid unwinds, DXY is firm, and that capital is funding the bid in growth, small-caps, and the early-cycle Consumer Cyclical rotation showing up in the Early-Runway radar.

The honest tension: under the bullish stance, momentum is cooling. SPY, QQQ, and Nasdaq all have MACD below signal with negative histograms despite trading above their moving averages — a classic late-leg condition where price is holding but the second derivative is rolling. The 10Y-2Y spread is compressing (-9.5% in 21d), Technology has flipped to a bearish MACD signal, and Communication Services and Energy are outright weak. The Dow leads with RSI 64 and a clean bullish MACD, which tells you leadership has rotated from mega-cap tech toward broader cyclical/value — consistent with the Early-Runway tilt into Apparel Retail, Travel Services, Resorts, and Industrials.

Net: stay long, hunt in the validated rotation pockets, but don't fade the momentum divergence. Confidence is capped at MEDIUM because price-trend and momentum indicators are pointing in different directions even though VIX is supportive.

active.name: Geopolitical Risk Unwind — Iran Deal / Hormuz Reopening
active.thesis: The Iran nuclear deal and the Strait of Hormuz reopening have resolved near-term crude supply-disruption risk. WTI crude has fallen approximately 5% to near $80/barrel as the geopolitical risk premium unwinds. This is unambiguously RISK-ON for equities: lower crude reduces input-cost and inflation-expectation pressure, eases the case for further Fed tightening, and removes the dominant macro tail-risk from the narrative. The correct read on oil weakness here is NOT 'Iran re-escalation risk' — it is the OPPOSITE: the Hormuz corridor is reopening and supply constraints are lifting. Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.
active.evidence: WTI crude ~$80 (-~5% from recent highs); crude trajectory shifting from HOLDING_BULLISH toward FADING_BULLISH/bearish. Natural gas divergence intact (independent supply story — not demand-driven). Broad commodity complex already fading (DBC, USO, BNO).

**[THE SPINE]** Dollar strength is the dominant force this week, and it is quietly reshaping every cross-asset relationship on the board. DXY is sitting at 99.65, above both its 21d and 50d SMAs, and the backtested DXY_METALS_TAG signal is ACTIVE — a regime where the inverse DXY/metals correlation (-0.45) has held in 70% of rolling 24-month windows. That is why Gold is down 4.4% on the month, Silver down 9.3%, and the entire precious-metals theme has been tagged FADING. The dollar is the spine; metals, commodities, and risk-on rotation are all hanging off it.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The regime is officially CHOPPY but transitional, with breadth healthy (72.7% of sectors above 50SMA, S&P breadth 52% bullish vs 20% bearish), VIX at 16.4 in clean contango (VIX3M 20.5), and the 10Y at 4.43 drifting lower on the day. Nothing here threatens the dollar-led tape — if anything, a soft VIX plus firm DXY plus rising 2Y (3.63, RSI 61) says the market is pricing resilience, not stress. Oil at 75.95 with RSI 30 and below the lower Bollinger band is in a downtrend, full stop — the backtest is explicit that WTI oversold has no mean-reversion edge (hit rate 51%, edge -3.87%), so do not call a bottom. Same discipline on TLT and the 10Y: both are trending, neither offers a reversion signal that holds.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is flowing into cyclicals and rate-sensitives that benefit from a firm-but-not-spiking dollar and a soft-landing read: XLF +6.4% on 21d leads, XLK +5.8% is accelerating bullish, IWM +5.5% is a confirmed leader, and XLV/XLI/XLB/XLRE all sit between +4.3% and +5.4% with leader tags. Rotation flows are pointed at Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and the AI Infrastructure theme (CHASING stage, day 16, health 8/10). What is conspicuously NOT being bought: precious metals miners, broad commodities, ag — all flipped bearish, consistent with the dollar spine.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The extended-and-dangerous bucket is clear: Semiconductors are 13 months hot with a +258% run that ties the 11-year record and carries an explicit CEILING flag — SMH/SOXX are exit-management territory, not entry territory. Semiconductor Equipment & Materials sits in the same spot (+288%, CEILING). The in-range, early-innings opportunity is Software - Infrastructure: only 1 month into a heat spell that typically runs 7, up just 3% vs a typical +18% — IGV and names tied to the AI software layer have runway the chip names no longer have. Internet Content & Information is also 1 month into a spell that typically runs 6, and is actually down 5% so far — early, not extended. Internet Retail (AMZN-led) is holding bullish with +13.7% on 21d, so it has moved but is not yet in ceiling territory.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** DXY 100.64 is the tripwire. A clean break above resistance accelerates the metals/commodity unwind and validates staying long the dollar-friendly cyclical-plus-software rotation; a rejection back below the 50SMA (~98.9) would crack the spine, give Gold/Silver room to bounce, and likely re-rate the entire FADING precious-metals theme. Secondary tell: SPY 760.4 resistance — through it, breadth confirms; rejection plus a VIX move back above 19.4 puts the CHOPPY regime label back to work.
